title: Connect a reader to a book
summary: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction.
introduction: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction. Your task: Identify the start and end nodes of READ.
learningObjectives: Identify the start and end nodes of READ.
Explain the example for connect a reader to a book

blocks.text: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction. Its type explains what that connection means.
Use Neo4j 5+ locally with Neo4j Browser or another Cypher editor. These queries use fictional cma-prefixed ids. Cypher is not SQL and does not run in this site's SQL playground.

blocks.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r1'}) SET r.name='Mia'
WITH r MATCH (b:Book {id:'cma-b1'}) MERGE (r)-[:READ]->(b) RETURN r.name,b.title;
blocks.title: Connect a reader to a book

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `MERGE` matches or creates the specified graph pattern. Use a stable identity pattern, then SET changing properties.
`MATCH` finds the described graph pattern. Labels and arrow direction narrow the connections being followed.

blocks.text: Mia is connected to Moon Trip by an outgoing READ relationship.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use a relationship type that describes the connection. Direction affects how a later pattern matches it.

blocks.text: Identify the start and end nodes of READ.
